sam_acme: Hey — our rerank calls started returning really odd scores this morning. All items come back with score 0.0 or identical values, ordering is basically random. No change on our side. Example request we send:
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "rerank-latest",
  "query": "pricing for enterprise",
  "documents": ["doc A", "doc B", "doc C"]
}
```
Response (truncated):
```
200 OK
{
  "results": [
    {"id":0, "score":0.0},
    {"id":1, "score":0.0},
    {"id":2, "score":0.0}
  ]
}
```
We saw this ~09:02 UTC. thread_ts:1903124567. Any ideas?

morgan_support: Sorry about that, really sorry. Can you paste the full response headers & the request id (X-Request-ID) if present? Also which region/tenant are you on? :eyes:

sam_acme: Thanks — tenant acme-prod, region us-west-2. X-Request-ID: req_0a9f3b2c. Headers: `x-model-resolved: rerank-legacy-2022` (found in internal trace we attached).

jordan_eng: Thanks — that header is telling. Looks like the alias `rerank-latest` resolved to `rerank-legacy-2022` for that request. That model was deprecated last quarter and should return proper scores, so weird. Can you share the exact body you sent (we need to check formatting/limits)?

sam_acme: Body above is exact. We also tried sending `rerank-2.0` directly and got correct scores. Only alias `rerank-latest` seems broken.

zoe_sre: pinging infra — @deploy-bot did we push any alias mappings or cache rollbacks around 09:00 UTC?

deploy-bot: config-change: alias-mapping update applied by ops@redwood at 2026-03-16T08:58:41Z. Changed `rerank-latest` -> `rerank-2.0`. Rolling propagation may cause older cached resolvers to still point at `rerank-legacy-2022` for ~5-10m.

jordan_eng: Ok that explains the alias flip. But that wouldn't cause all-zero scores unless the legacy model has a tokenization mismatch or there was an accidental eval-mode flag set. I'm going to check logs for req_0a9f3b2c.

jordan_eng: (log snippet) `model=rerank-legacy-2022; mode=eval; rerank_scores: computed but normalized to 0.0 due to divisor=0.0 in postproc` — looks like a postproc bug in the legacy model when fed inputs with >256 tokens after concatenation.

morgan_support: Have we confirmed the input sizes? Sam, do your documents or query exceed 256 tokens, or any very long html blobs?

sam_acme: Some docs are long (~1.5k words) — we usually trim server-side but a recent CI change removed the trimming for a subset of requests. We rolled that out yesterday.

zoe_sre: Combined cause then: 1) client switched to `rerank-latest` alias which briefly still resolved to legacy id in some edge caches, 2) legacy model has a known edge case with long concatenated inputs that resulted in postproc zero-division, 3) a recent client CI removed trimming so inputs hit the condition.
jordan_eng: Fix plan: Ops already ensured alias now consistently points to `rerank-2.0` globally. For safety we'll add a server-side hard guard in the legacy model pipeline to clamp the postproc divisor and return deterministic scores instead of 0.0.
morgan_support: Short-term workaround for you @sam_acme: explicitly set `model: "rerank-2.0"` in your requests (this bypasses alias resolution). Also re-enable document trimming to keep concat length < 1024 tokens.
sam_acme: Thanks — switching to `rerank-2.0` fixed it immediately on our side, confirmed ordering normal now. We re-enabled trimming and will monitor. :thumbsup:

jordan_eng: We'll deploy a hotfix to legacy postproc today (no downtime). I'll paste the PR once merged. Also adding improved monitoring alert for divisor=0 in postproc.
morgan_support: Apologies again for the outage. We'll follow up with a short incident note and notify customers who used the alias in the 08:50-09:10 UTC window.
sam_acme: Appreciate the quick help. Could you send the deprecation timeline for `rerank-legacy-2022` so we can audit our codebase?
zoe_sre: Yes — deprecation notice sent 2025-12-01, scheduled full retire on 2026-06-01. We'll DM you the link to the policy + migration guide.

jordan_eng: PR for hotfix: https://git.redwood.ai/r/infra/1234 — adding clamp and logging. ETA merge in 2h, rollout in next patch.
morgan_support: I'll keep this thread open until 24h of stable metrics. Thanks everyone. :heart:
